liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (3 reviews): Good Lovin' is called superb; Listener appreciates that Good Lovin' is left intact, not cut up, in this transfer [18][20][21]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Bird Song is a quiet, introspective performance, not as well played as versions from earlier shows [16]
- **Hard To Handle** (1 review): Hard To Handle is hot, though the extended Good Lovin' is judged even better [10]
- **I'm A King Bee** (1 review): King Bee in set two is one of only seven performed in 1971 [10]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight is called superb [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Pigpen Rap**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-02-24.sbd.cantor-crouch-diebert-gmb.87570.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 171 min; rated 3.56/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound quality and mix are lively, though Phil's bass is not prominent [16]
- **gd1971-02-24.sbd.clevenger.6190.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 146 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd71-02-24.sbd.orf.114.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 172 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds good: crisp and somewhat high in treble, but not shrill [11]
- **gd1971-02-24.sbd.clevenger.6189.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 146 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [5]

## Around the show

- After Casey Jones or Me And My Uncle, someone guesses the next song; uploader wonders if it is Marty Weinberg [7]
- Reviewer ranks it below the 2/19 and 2/23 nights of the six-night run; final night where Pigpen is turned loose [10]
- Pigpen and Janis Joplin Lovelight duet is pointed to the 6/7/69 show, which also has the first Dire Wolf [13]
- Reviewer thinks it is the weakest of the six-night run, subdued and less tightly played than earlier shows [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-02-24.sbd.cantor-crouch-diebert-gmb.87570.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer.; transferred by Transfer and mastering by Chris Ladner.; source: 7" two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A decoder > Apogee filter > analog in PCMF1/PCM501ES analog out >… [1]
- **gd1971-02-24.sbd.clevenger.6190.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf and Bob Clevenger; source: SBD -> Dolby A Reel -> Dolby A decode -> DAT -> Sound Forge NR -> CD-R [2]. Also: Sound Forge noise reduction attenuated a narrow band near 8000 Hz interference present on the original reels [2]
- **gd71-02-24.sbd.orf.114.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Via Leigh Orf; WBOTB source, with distortion removed digitally; a DAT clone from the 'whatever became of the bettys' tree [3]
- **gd1971-02-24.sbd.clevenger.6189.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Lee Orf;retracked by Bob Clevenger; source: SBD -> Dolby A Reel -> Dolby A decode -> DAT -> Sound Forge NR -> CD-R [5]. Also: Noise reduction applied to interference on source reels, as on the earlier uploaded Port Chester shows from 2/18 and 2/21 [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by crepuscularthad.blogspot.com: [Brokedown Palace: The Capitol Theatre and the Grateful Dead](https://crepuscularthad.blogspot.com/2017/03/capitol-theatre-and-grateful-dead.html) [23]
